conceptual assets.information: The JTAG TMS command bit controls TAP state transitions, which determine whether the DTM captures, shifts, updates, pauses or resets a debug access. Selecting the correct TAP state is required for reliable JTAG and DMI operation.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because changing TMS can select an unintended TAP state and cause the DTM to capture, shift or update the wrong register (lines 123-138, 178-197). Availability is at risk because holding or altering TMS can keep the TAP in reset or pause, preventing debug transfers from completing (lines 123-138).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter or hold jtag_tms_i so the TAP enters an unintended state, corrupting or blocking subsequent debug accesses.

conceptual assets.information: The decoded DMI operation command selects whether a DMI request is a read, write or no-operation. DMI request issuance and its direction depend on this command.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because changing the decoded operation can turn a DMI read into a write or otherwise issue the wrong request (lines 268-270, 283). Availability is at risk because selecting the no-operation command can suppress a required DMI transfer (lines 263-270).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the shifted DMI operation bits so the DTM issues an unintended request or suppresses a required read or write.

conceptual assets.information: The internal busy state records that a DMI request is outstanding and prevents the controller from accepting another DMI command until a response acknowledgement arrives. It has no direct entry or exit port because it is an internal transaction lock.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because modifying busy can clear an outstanding transaction early or permit an overlapping command, violating DMI transaction sequencing (lines 264-276). Availability is at risk because forcing busy high prevents the controller from accepting a new DMI command (lines 264-270).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force or clear the busy state to block DMI traffic or cause a new request to overlap an unfinished transaction.

conceptual assets.information: The DMI error status records that a DMI access was attempted while the controller was busy and is returned as part of the DMI response shifted through JTAG. Correct error reporting affects how the debug host handles DMI transactions.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because changing the error flag can make the DTM falsely report success or failure for a DMI access, and the flag is packed into the returned DMI response (lines 256-259, 229, 209).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the error status so the debug host accepts a failed access or treats a valid access as erroneous.

considered, not kept.reason: jtag_tck_i is a serial-link clock and rstn_i is a reset input, both excluded by the clocks-and-resets rule (lines 27-30, 94-102).

The shifted scan data is only forwarded through serial shift registers and debug-access stages between jtag_tdi_i, the DMI registers and jtag_tdo_o, so it is not this unit's information (lines 181, 194-210).

considered, not kept.reason: The address and write data are forwarded from the DMI shift register to the DMI request record without being decoded, stored as unit state or computed on by this unit (lines 266-267, 283-285).
The response data is copied from dmi_rsp_i.data into the shift response and then serialized, so forwarded-access stages exclude it as information of this unit (lines 274, 229, 189, 209).
dmi_rsp_i.ack is only a response handshake condition that clears the transaction lock, not an independent information piece (line 275).

The dmireset and dmihardreset controls are debug-transport control-register fields and only clear or control DMI error/reset behavior, so the debug-module and reset rules exclude them as separate concepts (lines 188, 219-221, 247-257).
tap_reg.ireg only selects which debug register or bypass path the debug port delivers, so it is excluded by the debug-module register rule (lines 178-197, 203-210).
tap_ctrl_state is a state machine state used only to order TAP steps and gate register operations, which the sequencing-state rule excludes as a concept of its own (lines 119-140, 178-212).
dr_trigger.sreg and dr_trigger.valid only detect and pace a DR_UPDATE event for subsequent DMI control processing, so the pacing-pulse rule excludes them (lines 149-161).
The IDCODE is formed from build-time generic identity values and is only shifted through the debug access port, so it has no shown security objective as a runtime asset (lines 21-23, 187, 207).
The bypass value is only a forwarded debug scan stage between the serial input and output and is not stored or computed as this unit's information (lines 190, 197, 210).

The synchronizer registers and edge-detection wires only resample JTAG inputs and generate timing conditions, so the clocks-and-resets, pacing and synchronizer rules exclude them as independent assets (lines 94-111).
